And al-Malik al-Adil, their uncle, went and made peace between them,
that Jerusalem should belong to al-Aziz,
and Jabala and Laodicea to al-Malik al-Zahir, the lord of Aleppo,
and to al-Adil certain villages in Egypt.
And they made peace,
and each one went to his own territory.
And in the year 591,
591 of the Arabs [1195 AD],
the Caliph al-Nasir sent an army with Sayf al-Din Tughril, one of his magnates, to Isfahan;
and the citizens surrendered it to him,
because they hated the Khwarazmian tyrants who had ruled over them.
And in this year also, al-Malik al-Aziz, the lord of Egypt, prepared
to come and take Damascus from al-Malik al-Afdal, his brother.
And when al-Afdal, his brother, heard this,
he went in person to the fortress of Ja'bar to al-Adil, his uncle,
and to al-Zahir, his brother,
and summoned them to his aid.
And they came with him to Damascus.
And al-Malik al-Aziz also came and encamped in the vicinity of Damascus.
Then the veteran servants of Saladin plotted against al-Malik al-Aziz,
and they sent to al-Adil and al-Afdal and said to them:
"Come out to us,
and we will deliver this man into your hands."
And when al-Aziz perceived the treachery,
he turned back in haste and swiftly to Egypt.
Then al-Adil and al-Afdal pursued him and entered Egypt,
and encamped against Bilbays.
And when they were able to conquer Egypt as well,
al-Adil held al-Afdal back,
and made peace;
and al-Afdal returned to Damascus,
and Jerusalem became his.
And al-Adil entered Egypt,
and became the administrator of the kingdom of al-Malik al-Aziz.
And in the year 592,
592 of the Arabs [1196 AD],
al-Malik al-Adil set out with al-Malik al-Aziz from Egypt,
and they came and encamped against Damascus to take it from al-Malik al-Afdal.
Now al-Afdal prepared for battle on the walls,
and divided the gates and towers among his nobles.
Then a certain man named Izz al-Din of Homs {OCR?}, who was guarding the gate called the Eastern Gate,
plotted against al-Afdal,
and let al-Adil into Damascus;
and he went and took up quarters in the court of Asad al-Din Shirkuh, his uncle,
and al-Malik al-Aziz also entered.
And they took the city from al-Malik al-Afdal,
and gave him the fortress of Salkhad,
and he departed and went away.
